title: Career Roadmap · Fabricator
summary: A Fabricator cuts, shapes, joins and assembles metal components into structures, frames, equipment, pipelines and industrial products using engineering drawings and workshop processes.

blocks.text: Primary pathway

items: ITI Welder / Fitter / Sheet Metal Worker

blocks.text: Core work
Read drawings • Measure and mark • Cut and form metal • Weld and assemble • Inspect dimensions and weld quality.

blocks.label: Recommended
blocks.text: Class 10 with Mathematics and Science; verify the chosen ITI trade’s entry rules.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Science in Classes 11–12 is useful but not always required for ITI entry.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: State ITI counselling or institute-specific admission.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Welding, structural steel, sheet-metal work, mechanical assembly and fabrication drawings.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Measurement, geometry, technical drawing, teamwork and workshop safety.

rows.text: Broader fabrication, production and quality roles

items: Fabrication, production or CAD-related roles, subject to employer requirements

blocks.text: Government / Public — investigate current trade availability

Recognized welding and fabrication training centres

blocks.text: Search and verify institutes through NCVT MIS and DGT. These are options to investigate, not confirmation that every institution offers a Fabricator course.

items.text: State ITI fee concessions and eligible government assistance.
Category-based scholarships, subject to scheme rules.
Apprenticeships that may provide a stipend.

blocks.text: Check the National Scholarship Portal and state scholarship portals. Eligibility depends on income, category, domicile and course/institute status. Verify current official notification.

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Workshop safety, engineering drawings, measuring, marking and hand tools.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Fabrication
blocks.text: Cutting, grinding, drilling, bending, fitting, welding and assembly.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced skills
blocks.text: Structural fabrication, dimensional inspection, welding quality, CNC cutting and CAD drawings.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Career preparation
blocks.text: Practical portfolio, supervised workshop experience, apprenticeship applications and trade assessments.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Fabricate a metal frame • Make a welded bracket • Assemble a small storage rack • Build a sheet-metal enclosure to drawing specifications.

blocks.label: Government / public sector
blocks.text: Railway workshops, defence manufacturing units and public-sector engineering facilities.

blocks.label: Private sector
blocks.text: Structural steel firms, shipyards, automotive suppliers, industrial equipment makers and HVAC fabrication companies.

blocks.label: Ideal training areas
blocks.text: Structural fabrication • Welding and fitting • Pipe fabrication • Sheet-metal assembly.
Find openings through Apprenticeship India. Availability and stipend depend on the employer and notification.

blocks.label: Common route
Specialist route
blocks.text: Fabricator → Structural / Pipe / Sheet-Metal Specialist.

blocks.label: Machine route
blocks.text: Fabrication experience + CNC training → CNC Cutting / Fabrication Machine Operator.

blocks.label: Design route
blocks.text: Fabrication experience + CAD skills → Fabrication CAD Technician, depending on employer requirements.

blocks.label: Further education
blocks.text: Eligible Mechanical Engineering diploma → Production, quality or fabrication supervision roles.
Relevant programs

blocks.label: Specializations
blocks.text: Structural steel • Pipe fabrication • Sheet-metal fabrication • Industrial equipment • Welding quality • CAD-based fabrication.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Construction, automotive, shipbuilding, railways, aerospace, HVAC, energy and heavy engineering.

blocks.label: Employer types
blocks.text: Manufacturing plants, fabrication workshops, infrastructure contractors, equipment manufacturers and engineering service companies.

blocks.label: Technical skills
blocks.text: Drawing interpretation, measurement, cutting, fitting, welding, assembly, dimensional accuracy and quality checks.

blocks.label: Tools / technologies
blocks.text: Welding machines, grinders, cutting equipment, drills, measuring instruments, CNC cutting machines and CAD software.
Useful credentials

items.text: DGT / NCVT-recognized certificate in a relevant ITI trade.
CAD/CAM, CNC and inspection training from recognized providers.

blocks.label: Countries to explore
blocks.text: Germany, Canada, Australia, UK and New Zealand.

blocks.label: Training routes
blocks.text: Recognized vocational colleges and technical institutes offering metal fabrication, welding, manufacturing technology or mechanical engineering.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Previous education or trade experience, practical assessment where applicable, language proficiency and study documentation. Qualification recognition varies by country and provider.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Metal Fabricator, Welder-Fabricator, Structural Fabricator, Pipe Fabricator and Fabrication Technician.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text:
Construction, manufacturing, mining, shipbuilding and industrial equipment.
